reproduction_target: Bacterial-isolate comparative-genomics characterization of two multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli strains (MBBL4, MBBL5) from bovine clinical mastitis milk in Gazipur, Bangladesh. The computational reproduction target is the downstream analysis of the two Illumina MiSeq 2x250 bp paired-end WGS datasets plus 28 NCBI reference genomes: (i) read QC (FastQC) and trimming (Trimmomatic); (ii) de novo assembly (SPAdes) and annotation (NCBI PGAP), completeness assessment (CheckM), subsystem counting (RAST web server), human-pathogen probability (PathogenFinder), circular-genome/COG visualization (GenoVi); (iii) mash-distance neighbour-joining phylogeny of 30 genomes (Mashtree) rendered in iTOL, ANI clustermap (ANIclustermap), pangenome analysis (Roary) and pangenome/core-genome curve fitting (PanGP); (iv) genome plasticity - regions of genomic plasticity (panRGP), insertion sequences (ISseeker), prophages (PHASTEST), plasmids (Platon); (v) resistome/virulome/genomic islands - CARD, VFDB + ecoli_VF via ABRicate, IslandViewer4. The physical wet-lab work (milk sampling, culture/biochemical/VITEK-2/16S identification, Kirby-Bauer antimicrobial susceptibility testing, DNA extraction/library prep/MiSeq sequencing) is data generation and is out of scope for computational reproduction; counted in W.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool from the bioRxiv v1 JATS full text. WebFetch returned HTTP 403 for the .source.xml, so the XML was retrieved with curl using a browser User-Agent and tag-stripped locally. NOTE ON FETCH HYGIENE: a first curl into a shared /tmp filename was overwritten mid-session by a concurrent process and briefly yielded a different manuscript (10.1101/2025.12.09.693261, the TNSEEK/Pectobacteriaceae paper); the assessment below is based on a re-fetch into an isolated directory whose text was verified to contain the MBBL4/MBBL5 mastitis content and the 683615 figure identifiers. The paper states NO code repository, NO scripts, NO workflow, and NO container/environment specification of its own; the only repository URL anywhere in the text is the third-party tool ABRicate (https://github.com/tseemann/abricate), which is a dependency, not the authors' analysis code. There is therefore no README to read at prose level. Version pins are dense but strictly per-tool and prose-only: FastQC v0.11.7, Trimmomatic v.0.39, SPAdes v.3.15.5, NCBI PGAP v.6.6, CheckM v1.2.3, RAST v.2.0, PathogenFinder v1.1, GenoVi v0.2.16, Mashtree v2.0, iTOL v7, ANIclustermap v.1.3.0, Roary v3.12.0, PanGP v1.0.1, CARD v4.0.1, VFDB v6.0, VITEK-2 v9.01 (instrument). Unversioned: panRGP, ISseeker, PHASTEST, Platon, IslandViewer4, ABRicate. Global parameter statement: 'All software were used with default parameters unless specified.' No RNG seed is given for the PanGP permutation sampling. Reference-genome identities live in supplementary Table S1, which was not opened at stage 1.

steps.label: Raw WGS read quality evaluation with FastQC v0.11.7 ('The quality of raw WGS reads was evaluated using FastQC v0.11.7'), applied to the Illumina MiSeq 2x250 bp paired-end reads of MBBL4 and MBBL5 deposited under BioProject PRJNA1171635; exact version pinned, defaults implied by the global 'default parameters unless specified' statement

Read trimming with Trimmomatic v.0.39 'for trimming Illumina adapters, known Illumina artifacts, phiX reads' - exact version pinned, but no adapter FASTA, no ILLUMINACLIP/SLIDINGWINDOW/MINLEN settings, and no phiX reference are stated

De novo genome assembly with SPAdes v.3.15.5 ('genome assembly was done with SPAdes v.3.15.5'), producing 125 contigs for MBBL4 and 71 for MBBL5, ~4.6 Mbp, GC 57.5%; exact version pinned, defaults implied (no k-mer list, no --careful/--isolate mode stated)

Genome annotation with the NCBI Prokaryotic Genome Annotation Pipeline v.6.6 (4,398 CDS in MBBL4, 4,385 in MBBL5); exact pipeline version pinned, but PGAP is a versioned service whose reference database snapshot is not identified in prose

Genome completeness/contamination estimation with CheckM v1.2.3 (98.53% / 0.27% for MBBL4; 99.56% / 0.70% for MBBL5); exact version pinned, defaults implied, but the CheckM marker-set database release is not stated

Subsystem counting with the RAST v.2.0 web server ('The RAST v.2.0 web-server was employed to count the number of subsystems'); version pinned but the invocation is a hosted web service - the executed code is not obtainable and the SEED subsystem database state at run time is not recorded

Human-pathogen probability prediction with PathogenFinder v.1.1 (scores 0.857 for MBBL4, 0.887 for MBBL5; 136 and 155 matched pathogenic gene families); version pinned, hosted service, threshold >0.80 stated in Results

Circular genome visualization and COG functional annotation with GenoVi v0.2.16 ('genomic visualization and functional annotation using Genovi v0.2.16'), yielding 25 COG categories over 4,678 (MBBL4) and 4,781 (MBBL5) genes; exact version pinned, defaults implied, COG database release not stated

Mash-distance-based neighbour-joining phylogeny of 30 E. coli genomes (MBBL4, MBBL5 plus 28 NCBI reference genomes listed in Table S1) with Mashtree v2.0; exact version pinned, defaults implied, but sketch size / k-mer size / bootstrap settings are not stated and the reference accession list sits in supplementary Table S1 rather than in the text

Tree rendering with iTOL v7 ('The tree was illustrated with iTOL v7'); version pinned, hosted web service, no annotation/colour-mapping files released so the published figure cannot be regenerated deterministically
Average nucleotide identity clustermap over all 30 genomes with ANIclustermap v.1.3.0; exact version pinned, defaults implied, underlying ANI backend (fastANI/skani) parameters not stated

Pangenome analysis of the 30 genomes with Roary v3.12.0 (13,571 genes: 2,983 core, 311 soft-core, 2,003 shell, 8,268 cloud); exact version pinned and the core/soft-core/shell/cloud prevalence bins are given explicitly, but the BLASTP identity threshold, the -e/-n alignment mode and the input annotation route (PGAP GFF vs Prokka) are not stated

Pangenome and core-genome curve fitting for 17 closely related genomes with PanGP v1.0.1 - distance guide algorithm, 100 replicates, 3,000 genome order permutations, power-law model y = Ax^B + C for pangenome size and exponential decay y = Ae^(Bx) + C for core genome; exact version and model forms pinned, but the sampling is stochastic and no RNG seed is reported, and the identity of the 17 selected genomes is only described as 'based on phylogenetic analysis'

Detection of regions of genomic plasticity (RGPs) in the 17 genomes with panRGP ('We used panRGP to detect the regions of genomic plasticity (RGPs)') - NO version pinned, no PPanGGOLiN parameters, no pangenome input specification

Insertion sequence identification with ISseeker ('and ISseeker to identify insertion sequences (ISs)') - NO version pinned, no IS reference database release stated, no identity/coverage thresholds given

Prophage region identification with PHASTEST ('Prophage regions and plasmids were identified by PHASTEST and Platon, respectively') - NO version pinned; PHASTEST is a hosted web service whose database state at run time is not recorded
Plasmid contig identification with Platon - NO version pinned, no Platon database release stated, no score/mode (--mode accuracy/sensitivity) given

Antibiotic resistance gene prediction for the 17 genomes with CARD v4.0.1 ('Antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) ... were predicted via CARD v4.0.1'); the CARD database version is pinned but the RGI software version, the RGI criteria (perfect/strict/loose) and the input mode (contig vs protein) are not stated

Virulence factor gene prediction with VFDB v6.0 and the ecoli_VF database 'in ABRicate (https://github.com/tseemann/abricate) tool with default parameter, applying a minimum coverage and identity threshold of >80%' - the VFDB database version is pinned and the coverage/identity threshold is explicit, but ABRicate itself carries NO version pin (bare repository URL, no commit, no release), so the invoking tool is unpinned

Genomic island prediction with IslandViewer4 ('Additionally, Islandviewer4 was used to predict genomic island of these selected genomes') - NO version/build pinned; hosted web service with an unrecorded reference-genome/database state and no stated island-predictor subset (IslandPath-DIMOB / SIGI-HMM / IslandPick)

headline.static_readiness: 0/20 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: RI ceiling on 14/20 computational steps (C1-C13 and C18), all of which name the invoked tool with an exact version in Methods prose (FastQC v0.11.7, Trimmomatic v.0.39, SPAdes v.3.15.5, PGAP v.6.6, CheckM v1.2.3, RAST v.2.0, PathogenFinder v1.1, GenoVi v0.2.16, Mashtree v2.0, iTOL v7, ANIclustermap v.1.3.0, Roary v3.12.0, PanGP v1.0.1, CARD v4.0.1). 6/20 steps cap at NI because the invoked tool carries no version at all (panRGP, ISseeker, PHASTEST, Platon, ABRicate, IslandViewer4); note that C19 pins the VFDB database at v6.0 but leaves the executing tool ABRicate floating, which is not sufficient for RI. No step reaches X: the two study genomes and their raw reads are public under BioProject PRJNA1171635 (assemblies JBINJR000000000.1 / JBINJQ000000000.1, 16S PV855738 / PV855739) and the 28 reference genomes are NCBI-derived (accessions listed in supplementary Table S1). The binding limitation is not data but code and environment: the paper releases NO analysis scripts, NO workflow, NO parameter files and NO environment specification of any kind, and six of the twenty steps run on hosted web services (RAST, PathogenFinder, iTOL, PHASTEST, IslandViewer4) whose database state at run time is unrecoverable. Even under stage-2 execution no step could exceed RI without a newly constructed environment capture, since nothing lockfile-, container- or release-shaped is claimed.
headline.coverage: 20 computational steps assessed from the bioRxiv v1 JATS full-text Methods prose. No repository landing page or README exists to read, because the paper states no code repository of its own. 4 physical wet-lab steps counted in W and not verdicted: (1) aseptic collection of 45 clinical-mastitis milk samples from 30 smallholder farms in Gazipur (Jan 2024 - May 2025) with EMB-agar isolation; (2) phenotypic/biochemical identification plus VITEK-2 v9.01 and 16S rRNA (UNI8f/uni1492r) confirmation; (3) Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion antimicrobial susceptibility testing of 33 isolates against 15 antibiotics per CLSI M100 34th ed., performed without replication; (4) QIAamp DNA Mini Kit extraction, Nextera DNA Flex library prep from 1 ng input, and Illumina MiSeq 2x250 bp paired-end sequencing.

gaps.missing: The paper states no code repository, no scripts, no workflow file and no supplementary code archive. There is no 'Code availability' statement at all; the 'Data availability' statement covers sequence deposition only ('The 16S rRNA gene sequences ... deposited in NCBI GenBank under accession numbers PV855738 and PV855739 ... The whole genome shotgun sequences for both strains are available in GenBank and the NCBI Sequence Read Archive (SRA) under BioProject accession PRJNA1171635. The genome versions reported in this study are JBINJR000000000.1 for MBBL4 and JBINJQ000000000.1 for MBBL5.'). The only repository URL anywhere in the manuscript is the third-party tool ABRicate (https://github.com/tseemann/abricate), which is a dependency and not the authors' analysis code. Consequently the exact commands, the ordering of the twenty tool invocations, the intermediate file handoffs and the figure/table generation code are all unavailable.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the command lines / driver scripts for the twenty analysis steps in a public repository, tag a release matching the manuscript, archive it to Zenodo or Software Heritage, and cite the resulting DOI or commit SHA in a Code availability statement.

gaps.missing: No environment lockfile, container image or digest, conda environment.yml, Bioconda channel/build pin, or module list is claimed anywhere in the manuscript. Version pins exist per tool in prose but there is no closure over interpreters, system libraries or transitive dependencies (e.g. the BLAST/CD-HIT/MCL stack under Roary v3.12.0, the fastANI/skani backend under ANIclustermap v.1.3.0, the Python/R stack under GenoVi v0.2.16 and PanGP v1.0.1). This is why every pinned step is capped at version=1 rather than 2.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a conda-lock/pixi lockfile or a container image referenced by digest that pins all twenty tools together with their interpreters and transitive dependencies.

gaps.where: C14 panRGP, C15 ISseeker, C16 PHASTEST, C17 Platon, C19 ABRicate, C20 IslandViewer4
gaps.missing: Six invoked tools are named with no version whatsoever, so the genome-plasticity section (RGPs, insertion sequences, prophages, plasmids), the virulence-gene screen and the genomic-island prediction cannot be pinned even at prose level. C19 is a specific hazard: the database is pinned (VFDB v6.0) while the tool that queries it (ABRicate) floats, and the paper does not state which ABRicate database snapshot of ecoli_VF was installed.
gaps.how_to_close: State the exact version/build of panRGP (or PPanGGOLiN), ISseeker, PHASTEST, Platon, ABRicate and IslandViewer4, and for each database-backed tool state the database release identifier as well as the tool version.

gaps.where: C2, C3, C9, C12, C13, C18 and all database-backed steps
gaps.missing: Parameters are covered by a single blanket sentence, 'All software were used with default parameters unless specified.' Specific unstated items: Trimmomatic adapter FASTA and clipping/quality/length settings; SPAdes k-mer list and assembly mode; Mashtree sketch/k-mer size and bootstrap; Roary identity threshold, alignment mode and input annotation source; PanGP RNG seed for the 100-replicate / 3,000-permutation sampling (no seed given anywhere) and the identity of the 17 selected genomes; RGI criteria and input mode for the CARD v4.0.1 screen. Reference-database snapshots (PGAP, CheckM marker sets, COG, CARD/RGI, VFDB/ecoli_VF, Platon, IS reference set) are not dated.
gaps.how_to_close: Report exact command lines including all non-default flags, publish the RNG seed for the PanGP sampling, list the 17 selected genome accessions in the main text, and record the download date and release identifier for every reference database used.

gaps.missing: There is no run-order documentation, no mapping from steps to figures and tables (Figs. 1A/1B, 2A/2B, 3A/3B, Tables 1-2 and Tables S1-S8 are not attributed to specific invocations), and no statement of which annotation output (PGAP GFF vs RAST vs GenoVi) feeds which downstream tool. Because no repository exists, there is also no README to carry this information.
gaps.how_to_close: Add a workflow diagram or driver script that names each step's inputs and outputs and maps each manuscript figure/table to the invocation that produced it.

gaps.where: C6 RAST v.2.0, C7 PathogenFinder v1.1, C10 iTOL v7, C16 PHASTEST, C20 IslandViewer4
gaps.missing: Five of twenty steps are executed on hosted web services. The executed code is not obtainable, the service-side database state at run time is not recorded, and no submission/job identifiers or downloaded result files are released, so these steps are not re-executable to a byte-identical result even if the service is still online. C10 additionally has no released annotation/colour-mapping files, so the published tree figure cannot be regenerated.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the raw output files returned by each web service as supplementary data with their run dates and job identifiers, and where a command-line equivalent exists (e.g. IslandPath-DIMOB, PHASTER/PHASTEST local install), use and pin the local version instead.

gaps.where: C9, C12, C13 - reference genome set
gaps.missing: The 28 NCBI reference genomes that define the phylogeny, the ANI clustermap and the 30-genome pangenome are listed only in supplementary Table S1, and the 17-genome subset used for PanGP, panRGP, ISseeker, PHASTEST, Platon, CARD, VFDB and IslandViewer4 is described qualitatively as 'closely related ... based on phylogenetic analysis' rather than enumerated in the text. Selection of the subset is therefore not machine-reconstructable from the manuscript body.
gaps.how_to_close: Enumerate both genome sets with their assembly accessions and versions in a machine-readable table in the main text or in a released manifest file, and state the objective criterion (e.g. ANI or mash-distance cutoff) used to select the 17.

gaps.missing: Milk sampling and E. coli isolation (45 samples / 30 farms), phenotypic + VITEK-2 v9.01 + 16S rRNA identification, Kirby-Bauer disc-diffusion antimicrobial susceptibility testing of 33 isolates against 15 antibiotics per CLSI M100 34th edition (explicitly 'performed without replication', and prevalence 'calculated based on observed frequencies without applying any statistical procedures'), and DNA extraction / Nextera DNA Flex library prep / Illumina MiSeq 2x250 bp sequencing. These are physical data-generation steps, out of scope for computational reproduction; counted in W (4), not verdicted. The absence of AST replication is a wet-lab reliability limitation, not a computational-readiness gap.
gaps.how_to_close: N/A for Tier-1 computational readiness; the reproducible computational entry point is BioProject PRJNA1171635 (raw reads and assemblies).
